name: Plausible

pricing.notes: Official pages checked 2026-07-30; Starter listed at $9/month and Business at $19/month in public plan references.
pricing.freeTier: No free plan, just a 30-day trial; the open source version is free to self-host.

tiers.name: Community Edition (self-hosted)
tiers.limits: Free software with no vendor-set site or traffic cap; hosting/database/operations are user-supplied.

tiers.name: Starter (up to 10k monthly pageviews/events)
tiers.limits: 1 website, 3 years of data retention and up to 10,000 combined pageviews/custom events per month.

tiers.name: Growth (up to 10k monthly pageviews/events)
tiers.limits: 3 websites, 3 team members, 3 years of retention and up to 10,000 combined pageviews/custom events per month.

tiers.name: Business (up to 10k monthly pageviews/events)
tiers.limits: 10 websites, 10 team members, 5 years of retention, 600 Stats API requests/hour and up to 10,000 combined pageviews/custom events per month.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom traffic; 10+ sites, 10+ team members, 600+ API requests/hour and 5+ years retention.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free hosted plan; 30-day no-card trial; Community Edition is free to self-host
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); hosted price scales by combined pageviews and custom events across all sites
pricing.hiddenCosts: Traffic brackets jump from 10,000 to 100,000 monthly events/pageviews. Separate Plausible teams are billed separately. After 2 consecutive over-limit months, Plausible asks for an upgrade and can lock dashboard access after a further week while collection continues; it does not publish an immediate per-event overage fee.

verdictSummary: Basic pageview/event analytics are easy, and Plausible's own code is open source; the paid value is hosted reliability, maintenance, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Add a small JS tracker, collect pageviews/events, aggregate by path/referrer/country/device, and show a dashboard.
whatYouLose: fast queries at millions of pageviews
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because analytics must be boring, fast, and legally safer without ops.

priorArt.name: plausible/analytics
priorArt.desc: Plausible itself is open source; self-host it

alternatives.name: GoatCounter
alternatives.desc: Even simpler than Plausible, which is either refreshing or a warning.

facts.install: Create a hosted account or run the single static binary or Docker image
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted instance uses SQLite by default or PostgreSQL; the hosted service stores analytics on GoatCounter's infrastructure and supports JSON and CSV exports
facts.gapVsPaid: It is even simpler, but gives up Plausible's more polished goals, revenue, funnels, team controls and reporting.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted use; self-hosting needs a reachable binary or container plus a public URL and TLS

alternatives.name: Plausible Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Plausible without the hosted bill; you keep the core dashboard and inherit the Compose stack.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose installer
facts.dataFormat: Account and configuration records live in PostgreSQL and analytics events live in ClickHouse on the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: It preserves the core dashboard but loses managed hosting, commercial support and cloud-only business features.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, roughly 2 GB of RAM, a domain with DNS and TLS, and backups for PostgreSQL and ClickHouse

alternatives.name: Rybbit
alternatives.desc: Plausible's core plus replay and funnels, in exchange for a busier dashboard.

facts.install: Use the hosted service or deploy the free self-hosted edition with Docker Compose
facts.dataFormat: The self-hosted stack uses PostgreSQL for application data, ClickHouse for analytics and Redis for queues and cache; hosted data lives in Rybbit's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: It is newer and busier, and replay and funnels add more privacy and operational surface than Plausible's deliberately narrow product.
facts.setupBlocker: The indefinitely free path is self-hosting, which requires Docker Compose, a domain, secrets and enough resources for three data services

alternatives.name: Umami
alternatives.desc: The closest broad substitute: simple traffic analytics, events and goals with your data attached.

facts.install: Create an Umami Cloud account or deploy the Node application with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted deployment stores analytics and account data in PostgreSQL; Umami Cloud stores it in Umami's managed service
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the closest broad substitute, but its conversion, revenue and reporting workflow is less mature and opinionated than Plausible's.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted signup; self-hosting requires Docker or Node hosting and a PostgreSQL database

notes: Script + ingest + dashboard is a weekend. The data pipeline polish; bot filtering, sessionization at scale; is the real product. Both are open source: self-hosting is the honest move here.
prompt:
Build me a privacy-first web analytics tool like Plausible (personal scale).
Requirements:

- A <2KB tracking snippet (vanilla JS, no cookies): sends pageview beacons with
  path, referrer, screen class, and a daily-rotating visitor hash computed
  server-side from IP + user-agent + a salt (never store raw IPs).
- An ingest endpoint that filters obvious bots by user-agent and writes to
  SQLite. One row per event; index on (site, date).
- A /dashboard (basic-auth from .env): unique visitors, pageviews, top pages,
  top referrers, and countries for today/7d/30d, with a visitors-per-day bar
  chart as inline SVG. Fast and clean, dark mode.
- Sessionization: a visit ends after 30 idle minutes; compute bounce rate.
- Multi-site support via a site id in the snippet.
- Node or Python, one process. Honest note in the README: at serious traffic,
  self-host the real Plausible instead · this is for personal sites.
